Select measurements by identifier or by position

Source: R/message-helpers.R
measurement_id.Rd

Wrap the measurements you pass to at = in rdm_sampling_covariance(), or to measurement = and highlight = in plot_views, to say whether the numbers are identifiers or row positions.

Usage

measurement_id(x)

measurement_position(x)

Arguments

x

For measurement_id(), one or more measurement identifiers, numeric or character, exactly as a view's measurement column prints them (equivalently, values of the frame's $index$measurement). For measurement_position(), one or more whole-number row positions.

Value

A classed selector, crossform_measurement_id or crossform_measurement_position, holding x. It is resolved against the frame or view it is passed with; an identifier the frame does not carry, or a position outside 1..n, is an input error.

Details

Every compiled frame names its measurements twice. The identifier is the frame's $index$measurement, carried into each view as $index and printed in the view's measurement column: domain feature ids for voxelwise() and searchlights() (the full-volume voxel indices of a masked volume_domain()), region labels for regions(), and "family::node" for a frame_family(). The position is the row of the frame's $weights and of the view's values, 1..n: what which.max(view$total) or order(view$total) returns.

On an abstract_domain() with default ids, or a volume without holes, the two coincide and a bare number works either way. When the identifiers are whole numbers that differ from the positions – any masked volume – a bare number is ambiguous: 117 copied from a printed view is voxel 117, but as a position it is some other voxel. crossform does not guess. It refuses a bare number there, and asks for one of:

  • measurement_id(117), or the character identifier "117": the measurement printed as 117.

  • measurement_position(which.max(view$total)): the row position.

Identifiers that are not whole numbers (region names, "family::node") cannot be mistaken for positions, so bare numbers stay positions there.

See also

Other sampling uncertainty: rdm_sampling_covariance(), reconstruct_evidence(), sampling_capabilities(), sampling_covariance()

Examples

mask <- array(TRUE, c(4L, 4L, 2L))
mask[1:2, , 1] <- FALSE
domain <- volume_domain(mask, spacing = c(3, 3, 3), id = "masked")
frame <- compile_frame(searchlights(3.1), domain)

# Identifiers are full-volume voxel indices; positions are rows 1..n.
head(frame$index$measurement)
#> [1]  3  4  7  8 11 12

# The same measurement, named both ways.
measurement_id(11)
#> <measurement_id> 11
measurement_position(match(11, frame$index$measurement))
#> <measurement_position> 5
